items.answer: Registration is the step in the tracking process that estimates the initial position and orientation of the sensor or user, so the starting point is known before movement is tracked, and sets the initial alignment between the real and virtual worlds. It may be aided by fiducial markers, reflectors, or tags, or performed without them using computer vision.

An inertial measurement unit (IMU) is a self-contained composite hardware unit that mainly contains a gyroscope, accelerometer, and magnetometer to measure changes in orientation, translation velocity, or acceleration rather than absolute values.
A gyroscope is an inertial sensor that captures angular velocity. In an inertial measurement unit, it is a main component, and sensor tracking relies mainly on its readings.
An accelerometer is an inertial sensor that captures linear acceleration along the x, y, and z axes, and in an inertial measurement unit its readings can be used to detect drift errors.
A magnetometer is a sensor that captures magnetic field strength along the x, y, and z axes and can be used to detect drift errors in tracking.

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.

questions.question: What is included in the others category for VR and AR tracking technologies?
options: Electromagnetic and acoustic or ultrasonic tracking technologies
Electromechanical and inertial tracking technologies
Location-based and hybrid tracking technologies
Inertial and vision-based tracking technologies
questions.explanation: In the VR and AR tracking taxonomy, the others category contains location-based and hybrid tracking, while inertial, vision-based, electromagnetic, acoustic or ultrasonic, and electromechanical are main tracking families.

data.text: Virtual reality and augmented reality tracking is organized into several technology families. These families include electromechanical, electromagnetic, acoustic/ultrasonic, vision-based, and inertial methods, with location-based and hybrid methods placed in the broader others category.
points: Virtual reality and augmented reality tracking technologies are categorized into electromechanical, electromagnetic, acoustic/ultrasonic, vision-based, inertial, and others, including location-based/hybrid.

questions.question: What physical arrangement forms an electromechanical tracker?
options: an ultrasonic speaker and a head-mounted microphone
a serial or parallel kinematic structure
a magnetic transmitter and a mobile receiver
a camera and a bright infrared target
questions.explanation: Electromechanical trackers are built from linked, jointed kinematic chains. Magnetic transmitters, ultrasonic speakers, and cameras belong to other tracking methods, not to the kinematic structure of an electromechanical tracker.

questions.question: Which description matches a world-fixed electromechanical tracker?
options: a body-worn frame used to move an animated avatar
a microphone paired with a stationary ultrasonic speaker
a display attached to a mechanically pivoted tracked setup
a receiver attached to a headset and moved through magnetic fields
questions.explanation: A world-fixed electromechanical tracker pairs a display with a tracked setup that has mechanical pivoting. The body-worn frame describes a wearable tracker, while magnetic receivers and ultrasonic microphones belong to other tracking methods.

questions.question: What practical drawback is associated with wearable electromechanical trackers?
options: They are limited by ambient light for optical targets
They are limited by line of sight to ultrasonic transmitters
They are not very comfortable and are quite cumbersome
They are fixed to a display with a counterbalance
questions.explanation: Wearable electromechanical trackers are not very comfortable and are quite cumbersome, and they are used in limited, highly specialized setups. A counterbalanced display belongs to a world-fixed setup, while line-of-sight and ambient-light concerns belong to ultrasonic and optical tracking.

data.text: Electromechanical trackers are mechanical structures of links and sensor joints, and they come in world-fixed and wearable forms. The world-fixed form is a cumbersome display-attached mechanism. The wearable form translates a person's movements into animated avatar movement, while also being uncomfortable, cumbersome, and used in limited, highly specialized setups.
points: Electromechanical trackers consist of serial or parallel kinematic structures of links interconnected by joints with sensors.
Electromechanical trackers are of two types: world-fixed trackers and wearable trackers.
World-fixed electromechanical trackers are cumbersome setups with a display attached to a tracked structure with pivoting, sensors, and counterbalance.
Wearable electromechanical trackers are body-worn and translate a person's movements into animated avatar movement within a virtual world.
Wearable electromechanical trackers are not very comfortable to wear, are quite cumbersome, and are used in limited, highly specialized setups.

questions.question: How does an electromagnetic tracker obtain the real-time position of a headset?
options: By comparing images from cameras that watch a marker
By timing ultrasonic pulses between the speakers and microphones
By measuring joint angles in a mechanical linkage
By reading currents induced in the receiver by magnetic fields
questions.explanation: An electromagnetic tracker uses magnetic fields from a stationary transmitter to induce currents in a receiver on the headset, and those signals are used to determine position. The other options describe ultrasonic, vision-based, or electromechanical tracking instead.

questions.question: In acoustic head tracking, what is the role of the hardware attached to the HMD?
options: It sends ultrasonic signals as a speaker
It produces magnetic fields as a transmitter
It receives ultrasonic signals as a microphone
It captures visible-light images as a tracking camera
questions.explanation: In acoustic or ultrasonic tracking, the headset-mounted hardware is a receiver, which can be called a microphone, while the stationary transmitters are the speakers. Sending ultrasonic signals is the role of the stationary transmitter, not the headset hardware.

questions.question: Why can an electromagnetic tracker keep locating a headset when an obstacle lies between the transmitter and the headset?
options: It sends stronger ultrasonic signals around the obstacle
It uses visible-light cameras to see around the obstacle in the environment
It does not need line of sight between transmitter and receiver
It keeps the receiving unit fixed in the environment
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic tracking does not require an unobstructed path between the transmitter and the receiver, unlike acoustic or ultrasonic tracking. Ultrasonic tracking needs line of sight, so stronger sound would not remove the obstruction problem.

data.text: Electromagnetic and acoustic or ultrasonic trackers estimate a head’s real-time position using signals between transmitters and receivers. Electromagnetic tracking uses magnetic fields, while acoustic or ultrasonic tracking uses ultrasonic signals. Although both use stationary transmitters and receivers that move with the head or body, acoustic tracking needs line of sight and electromagnetic tracking does not.
points: Non-contact electromagnetic trackers estimate head position from magnetic fields, generally using three orthogonal fields that induce AC or DC currents.
Acoustic or ultrasonic tracking determines real-time head position using ultrasonic signals from transmitters to HMD microphones.
Electromagnetic and acoustic or ultrasonic trackers both use stationary transmitters and receivers that move with the head or body.
Acoustic or ultrasonic tracking requires line of sight, whereas electromagnetic tracking does not require this line of sight.

questions.question: What does a vision-based tracker determine for a tracked object?
options: Joint rotation angles
Magnetic field direction
Ultrasonic travel time
Position and orientation
questions.explanation: Vision-based trackers determine poses, such as position and orientation, using optical sensors or cameras. Magnetic field direction, ultrasonic travel time, and joint angles belong to other tracking approaches.

questions.question: Why are targets used in infrared tracking easy to detect?
options: They generate magnetic fields that are stronger than the surroundings
They display fiducial patterns that are sharper than the surroundings
They emit or reflect light that is brighter than the surroundings
They emit ultrasonic pulses that are louder than the surroundings
questions.explanation: Infrared tracking targets emit or reflect light, which gives them high brightness compared with the surroundings and makes them easier to detect.

questions.question: Why is infrared tracking less affected by poor ambient lighting or harsh shadows?
options: It relies on visible-light signals rather than infrared signals
It relies on infrared signals rather than visible-light signals
It relies on outside-in cameras rather than inside-out cameras
It relies on emitted targets rather than reflected targets
questions.explanation: Infrared tracking is robust to adverse illumination effects because it uses infrared sensing rather than visible-light sensing. Camera placement and whether targets emit or reflect are not the reason for this robustness.

questions.question: What is true of outside-in infrared tracking?
options: Its cameras are in the environment and detect the tracked object without attached targets
Its cameras are in the environment and detect targets on the tracked object
Its cameras are on the user and detect targets in the environment
Its cameras are on the tracked object and detect targets in the environment
questions.explanation: In outside-in infrared tracking, environment-placed cameras detect targets attached to the tracked object to determine pose and position. Inside-out tracking instead uses a camera mounted with the user to detect external targets.

data.text: Vision-based trackers estimate pose with optical sensors or cameras; the main optical sensor categories are infrared, visible light, and 3D structure sensors. Infrared tracking is an early VR/AR method; it uses bright emitting or reflecting targets, which are easy to detect, and can tolerate adverse illumination such as poor lighting or shadows. It can be configured outside-in, with environment cameras detecting attached targets, or inside-out, with a user-mounted camera detecting external targets, to estimate pose.
points: Vision-based trackers are more prevalent trackers that use optical sensors or cameras to determine poses.
Infrared, visible light, and 3D structure sensors are the three main optical sensor categories for detecting or tracking pose.
Infrared tracking is among the earliest vision-based tracking techniques developed and used in VR or AR.
Infrared tracking uses bright emitting or reflecting targets and is robust to adverse illumination, such as poor lighting or shadows.
Infrared tracking can be outside-in, with environment cameras detecting attached targets, or inside-out, with a user-mounted camera detecting external targets.

questions.question: What makes optical cameras a practical sensor choice for visible light tracking?
options: Their use of infrared targets attached to the tracked object
Their availability mainly in dedicated augmented reality headsets
Their abundance in consumer-grade electronic devices
Their need for small colored LEDs attached to the tracked object
questions.explanation: Visible light tracking often uses optical cameras because such cameras are already common in many consumer devices. Infrared targets and colored LEDs are not required by optical cameras themselves.

questions.question: What is the role of fiducials in fiducial tracking?
options: They aid registration and tracking of the tracked object
They replace the optical camera used for the tracked object
They are features already present in the tracked object
They eliminate the need to register the tracked object
questions.explanation: Fiducials are artificial landmarks added to help register and track an object. They do not replace the camera, and they are not natural features already present in the scene.

questions.question: Which fiducial type supports detection at greater distances?
options: A multi-ring fiducial
A constant width ring fiducial
A proportional width ring fiducial
A small colored LED fiducial
questions.explanation: Multi-ring fiducials are used for detection at greater distances. Proportional and constant width ring fiducials differ in how their appearance or ring width behaves with distance, and small colored LEDs are another kind of fiducial.

data.text: Visible light tracking uses visible light sensors or optical cameras, with optical cameras available in almost all consumer-grade electronics. It includes fiducial, natural feature, and model-based tracking. Fiducial tracking adds artificial landmarks to the environment to support registration and tracking, and its complexity depends on the fiducial type.
points: Visible light tracking uses visible light sensors or optical cameras, the most common optical sensors in almost all consumer-grade electronics.
Visible light tracking has three techniques: fiducial, natural feature, and model-based tracking.
Fiducial tracking adds artificial landmarks to the environment to aid registration and tracking of an object.
Fiducial tracking complexity depends on the kind of fiducial used.

questions.question: What does the second category of visual light-based sensing use to register camera pose in real time?
options: A map updated in the environment
Features already present in the environment
Artificial landmarks added to the environment
Gestures made in the environment
questions.explanation: Natural feature tracking, the second category, registers camera pose using features already present in the environment. Adding artificial landmarks corresponds to fiducial tracking, while a map describes SLAM and gestures are not the tracked input.

questions.question: In natural feature tracking, what is the purpose of calculating a unique descriptor for each detected feature?
options: To determine which points, corners, and line intersections are present
To make the detected features unique to the surroundings
To identify and differentiate one feature from other features
To compute the camera pose directly from a single feature
questions.explanation: A descriptor is calculated to tell one detected feature apart from another. Detecting points, corners, and line intersections is a separate step, and pose estimation comes from matching features rather than from a single descriptor alone.

questions.question: How is the camera pose estimated in the tracking method that relies on details already visible in the surroundings?
options: By matching scene features with object features using their descriptors
By matching scene features with rendered views using their pixels
By matching scene features with depth maps using their distances
By matching scene features with stored models using their shapes
questions.explanation: The camera pose is estimated by matching features detected in the scene with features detected on the object, using their calculated descriptors. Matching against stored models, depth maps, or rendered views describes other mechanisms, not this tracking method.

data.text: Natural feature tracking is a visual light-based method that estimates a camera’s pose in real time from features already present in the environment. It relies on computer vision to detect unique features in the surroundings and to calculate unique descriptors that identify and differentiate them. These descriptors are then matched between the scene and the tracked object, giving the camera pose estimate.
points: Natural feature tracking is a visual light-based method that registers camera pose in real time from natural features.
Natural feature tracking’s computer vision algorithms detect unique features in the surroundings of the tracked object.
Natural feature tracking calculates unique descriptors for each detected feature to identify and differentiate one from the others.
Natural feature tracking estimates camera pose by matching scene feature descriptors with object feature descriptors.

activities.title: Order the stages of natural feature tracking

items.title: Order the stages of natural feature tracking
steps: Unique features such as points, corners, and line intersections are detected
Unique descriptors are calculated for each detected feature
Camera pose is estimated by matching scene features with object features using descriptors

questions.question: What does SLAM do to support real-time tracking of an unknown environment?
options: It adds fiducials to the scene to localize the object within it
It waits for a full model to localize the object within it
It uses a pre-existing map to localize the object within it
It creates and updates a map while localizing the object within it
questions.explanation: SLAM builds and revises a map of the environment at the same time as it determines the object's changing position. A pre-existing map, fiducials, or a completed model is not required for the simultaneous process.

questions.question: How does PTAM differ from SLAM in its handling of tracking and mapping?
options: It handles camera tracking and environment mapping as one fixed combined activity
It handles camera tracking and stored-model matching as separate activities
It handles fiducial matching and environment mapping as separate activities
It handles camera tracking and environment mapping as separate activities
questions.explanation: PTAM is an optimization of SLAM that separates camera tracking from environment mapping into distinct activities. It does not merge those activities, nor replace them with fiducial or stored-model matching.

questions.question: What outcome is stated for PTAM compared with SLAM?
options: Improved tracking accuracy and overall performance
A greater need for fiducials in the environment
Reduced tracking accuracy and overall performance
A greater need for a pre-existing map of the environment
questions.explanation: PTAM is described as improving both tracking accuracy and overall performance. It is not described as degrading performance or increasing dependence on fiducials or pre-existing maps.

questions.question: Why is PTAM more suitable for smaller environments?
options: Because its drift-free tracking of unknown environments becomes unreliable in larger environments
Because it needs fiducial markers visible in larger environments
Because its computational requirements are quite high in larger environments
Because it needs a pre-existing map of larger environments
questions.explanation: PTAM is more suitable for smaller environments because larger environments impose quite high computational requirements. Drift-free tracking does not make it more suitable, and it does not require fiducial markers or a pre-existing map.

data.text: Model-based tracking is the third category of visible light-based sensing. SLAM, originally developed for robot navigation and later adapted for augmented reality, creates and updates a map while localizing changing positions, enabling drift-free real-time tracking of unknown environments. PTAM is a further SLAM optimization designed for augmented reality; it separates tracking and mapping, improving tracking accuracy and overall performance, though it is more suitable for smaller environments because larger environments have quite high computational requirements.
points: Model-based tracking is the third category of visible light-based sensing.
SLAM simultaneously creates and updates a map while localizing changing positions, enabling real-time tracking.
Originally developed for robot navigation and adapted for augmented reality, SLAM allows drift-free tracking of unknown environments.
PTAM is a further SLAM optimization designed for augmented reality, separating tracking and mapping, improving tracking accuracy and overall performance.
PTAM is more suitable for smaller environments because larger environments have quite high computational requirements.

questions.question: Which output is characteristic of 3D structure tracking?
options: Images built from point positions
Poses built from point positions
Markers built from point positions
Models built from point positions
questions.explanation: 3D structure tracking creates 3D models of structures in the environment from sensed point positions; it does not directly create images, markers, or pose estimates.

questions.question: What recent hardware trend made 3D structure tracking more usable?
options: Commercial 3D structure markers became affordable
Commercial 3D structure sensors became affordable
Commercial 3D structure trackers became affordable
Commercial 3D structure displays became affordable
questions.explanation: Commercial sensors that detect 3D structure information became affordable, making 3D structure tracking more usable; markers, displays, and trackers are not the hardware trend described.

questions.question: In an AR system that creates 3D models from a structured-light depth sensor, what else can those models be used for?
options: Replacing the image from the sensor
Generating markers around the sensor
Tracking the pose of the sensor
Reducing the need for the sensor
questions.explanation: The 3D models can also be used to track the sensor's pose; they are not a substitute for the sensor's image data, a source of markers, or a way to remove the sensor.

data.text: 3D structure tracking creates 3D models of real structures from 3D point positions obtained with commercial sensors, and those models support augmenting the real-world view. The sensors used for this technique became affordable, beginning with Microsoft Kinect. Kinect Fusion illustrates the approach by turning Kinect structured-light depth data into 3D models that also track the Kinect's pose.
points: 3D structure tracking uses commercial sensors to obtain 3D point positions and create 3D models for augmenting real-world views.
Commercial sensors capable of detecting 3D structure became affordable, a trend started by Microsoft Kinect, with similar devices available.
Kinect Fusion creates 3D models from Kinect structured-light depth data and uses those models to track the Kinect's pose.

questions.question: What do inertial trackers report?
options: Absolute-distance readings from a fixed base station
Absolute-value readings for orientation, velocity, or acceleration
Absolute-position readings for the surrounding room
Rate-of-change readings for orientation, velocity, or acceleration
questions.explanation: Inertial trackers measure changes such as orientation, translation velocity, or acceleration, rather than absolute values. They do not by themselves provide absolute position or distance from a fixed reference.

questions.question: Why are inertial trackers readily usable on smartphones and head-mounted displays?
options: They are built into the device but have a short range limitation
They rely on external beacons and have a room-scale limitation
They are built into the device and have no range limitation
They rely on GPS satellites and have an outdoor coverage limitation
questions.explanation: Inertial trackers are typically MEMS-based sensors inside the user's device, so they can be used readily without an external tracking range. They do not depend on beacons or GPS for basic tracking.

questions.question: Why might GPS be used in a hybrid XR tracking system?
options: It can provide full body pose when precise position is not needed
It can provide precise indoor position when precise position is needed
It can provide approximate outdoor position when precise position is not needed
It can provide head orientation when precise position is not needed
questions.explanation: GPS is useful outdoors and is appropriate when an approximation is enough or as part of a hybrid system. It is generally less accurate indoors and provides only positional tracking, not orientation or full pose.

questions.question: What does real-time kinematic technology add to a basic global positioning system sensor?
options: Carrier-wave measurements that improve detection accuracy
Magnetometer measurements that improve outdoor accuracy
Camera-feature measurements that improve tracking accuracy
Acoustic-ranging measurements that improve indoor accuracy
questions.explanation: RTK improves basic global positioning system positioning by using signal carrier waves for measurement, giving better accuracy. It is not based on acoustic-ranging, magnetometer, or camera-feature measurements.

data.text: Built-in inertial tracking and positional GPS provide different kinds of tracking data. Inertial sensors measure changes and can be combined in software into hybrid sensors, while GPS works outdoors but is position-only and often inaccurate indoors. RTK can improve GPS accuracy, and GPS is typically used when approximation suffices or it is part of a hybrid tracking system.
points: Inertial trackers are MEMS-based, self-contained device sensors that measure changes, not absolute values, without range limits.
Hybrid software-level sensors can be part of devices using gyroscope, accelerometer, and magnetometer.
Basic tracking sensors include electromechanical, electromagnetic, inertial, 3D structure, and light-based sensing, unlike acoustic or GPS.
GPS is useful outdoors, gives only position, and generally has low accuracy, especially indoors.
RTK improves basic GPS accuracy using GPS carrier waves, while GPS fits approximate or hybrid tracking needs.

questions.question: Why is motion capture not fundamentally new?
options: It can be processed as a non-real-time recording approach
It can be mounted as a display-based gaze approach
It can be based on any existing sensing approach
It can be packaged as a full body suit approach
questions.explanation: Motion capture is not fundamentally new because it can use an existing sensing approach to record movement. The other options describe packaging, timing, or display-mounted gaze capture, not why it is not a new basic approach.

questions.question: What can be true about the timing of motion capture?
options: It may be rendered through a lens placed near the eyes
It may be conveyed by a platform that moves the whole body
It may be processed after the movements are recorded
It may be felt as vibrations through a haptic device
questions.explanation: Motion capture does not have to happen while the user is moving; it may be handled after the movements have been recorded. The other options describe VR output devices, not the timing of motion capture.

questions.question: What do eye-tracking systems typically track?
options: The user's full body movement
The 3D positions of points in a scene
The change in orientation of a device
The user's gaze point or area of the gaze
questions.explanation: Eye-tracking systems usually follow where the user is looking. Full body movement, scene structure, and device orientation are tracked by other methods.

questions.question: What is a hybrid tracker in XR tracking?
options: A wearable suit that records full body movement and typically performs better
A method that combines basic tracking systems and typically performs better
A high-resolution camera that tracks the gaze point and typically performs better
A method that uses one basic tracking system and typically performs better
questions.explanation: A hybrid tracker combines two or more basic tracking approaches, and such combinations are typically found to perform better than single-technology tracking. A single sensor, a full body suit, or a gaze camera alone does not define a hybrid tracker.

data.text: Motion capture and eye tracking track movement and gaze, while hybrid tracking combines basic tracking methods. Motion capture records real-world movement, typically through wearable suits, and can be real-time or non-real-time. Eye tracking observes the gaze point or area using optical, infrared lighting, EOG, or VOG methods, with systems head-mounted, display-attached, or part of other trackers. Hybrid trackers combine two or more basic tracking methods and typically outperform single-technology trackers.
points: Motion capture is not a fundamentally new tracking method; it can be based on any tracking method.
Motion capture is typically packaged as wearable suits with tracking sensors and need not be real-time.
Eye-tracking systems can be head-mounted, display-attached, or built into other trackers, using optical, infrared lighting, EOG, or VOG methods.
Eye-tracking systems typically track the user's gaze point or gaze area.
Hybrid trackers combine two or more basic tracking methods and typically outperform single-technology trackers.

questions.question: Why can an electromagnetic tracker estimate a receiver's position when obstacles block the transmitter-receiver path, while an acoustic tracker cannot?
questions.reference_answer: Electromagnetic tracking does not require line of sight between transmitter and receiver, whereas acoustic tracking does. Both rely on stationary transmitters and receivers that move with the head or body. Electromagnetic trackers obtain the receiver's real-time position from the direction of the magnetic field, while acoustic tracking uses ultrasonic signals to determine the receiver's position, so an obstacle blocks the acoustic measurement.

questions.question: Why is parallel tracking and mapping considered an optimization of simultaneous localization and mapping that is more suitable for smaller than larger environments?
questions.reference_answer: PTAM is an SLAM optimization because it separates camera tracking from environment mapping. SLAM creates and updates a map while localizing, but PTAM's separate activities improve tracking accuracy and performance. It is more suitable for smaller environments because its computational requirements for larger ones are quite high.

questions.question: Why is the global positioning system more useful as part of a hybrid tracking system than as the only tracking method for an XR system?
questions.reference_answer: The global positioning system is more useful in a hybrid tracking system because GPS generally offers low accuracy and allows only positional tracking, while a hybrid tracker uses two or more basic tracking systems and typically performs better than single-technology-based tracking. GPS is typically used when accurate position registration is not important, when an approximation is good enough, or as part of a hybrid system.
